items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I have to say somebody that’s almost a perfect example of somebody who has his own sound and obviously is a wonderful saxophone player but it ain’t telling us nothing is Kenny G as a good example.

ctx.x: Where does that come from? How do you teach that?

That comes from elevating the idea, the concept of get your own voice, regardless of what you’re going to do with it. Because they used to say look, anybody can practice, anybody can become somewhat proficient on an instrument, I mean if you have any kind of musical talent. It’s not a question of whether or not you really use this entire amount of information that you’ve not gotten from practicing in order to run your scales and run all this fancy stuff around. I mean I have to say somebody that’s almost a…

sound that he obviously has taken time on. I heard him play tenor one time on a record and it was very interesting because it’s like he’s using the same format, the same template and the same sound actually in a tenor. I mean it just sounds like Kenny G playing tenor.
